Any degree. JE needs B.E./B.Tech. Age 18–30 (CGL), 20–25 (CPO).

stages.name: Tier 1 (CBT)
stages.tests: 100 Qs, 60 min. Reasoning, GK, Quant, English. 200 marks.
stages.note: Qualifying. Negative marking 0.50. Cut-off varies by post and category.

stages.name: Tier 2 (CBT)
stages.tests: 200 Qs, 2 hrs. Quant, English, GK, Reasoning. + Computer (qualifying).
stages.note: Merit prepared from Tier 2. Descriptive paper (essay + letter) for some posts.

stages.name: Skill Test / Typing
stages.tests: Typing: 35 wpm English / 30 wpm Hindi (10 min). DEST for DEO.
stages.note: Qualifying only. No marks added to merit.

stages.name: Document Verification
stages.tests: All originals, caste, domicile, NOC, gap certificate.
stages.note: Any discrepancy = rejection. Verify before applying.

reality: SSC CGL is the most popular government exam. 20-30 lakh applicants for 7000-15000 vacancies.
Tier 1 is qualifying but the cut-off is high. Focus on accuracy, not just speed.
CHSL and CGL have different syllabi. CHSL is easier but fewer vacancies.
GD Constable has physical tests (running, long jump, high jump). Start fitness early.
SSC exams have a fixed calendar. CGL in Aug-Sep, CHSL in Mar-Apr, MTS in Sep-Oct.
Job posting: Income Tax (CBDT) and Customs (CBIC) are most sought after in CGL.

faq.q: What is the difference between SSC CGL and SSC CHSL?
faq.a: CGL = Combined Graduate Level (graduate posts: Inspector, Auditor, ASO). CHSL = Combined Higher Secondary Level (12th pass posts: Clerk, DEO, PA). Different eligibility, different exams.

faq.q: Can a 12th pass apply for SSC CGL?
faq.a: No. CGL requires graduation. 12th pass can apply for CHSL, MTS, GD Constable, and Stenographer.

faq.q: What is the age limit for SSC exams?
faq.a: MTS: 18-25 years. CHSL: 18-27 years. CGL: 18-30 years (varies by post). CPO: 20-25 years. GD Constable: 18-23 years. Age relaxations for SC/ST/OBC/PwD.
No attempt limit for SSC exams (age-based). You can apply as long as you meet the age criteria.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in SSC exams?
faq.a: Yes. Tier 1: 0.50 per wrong answer. Tier 2: 0.25 per wrong answer (varies by paper). No negative marking in skill test or typing.

faq.q: Where do I find official SSC notifications?
faq.a: ssc.gov.in (main site) and regional SSC websites. SarkariJobs+ links the official notification PDF on every listing page.
